body:
Thank you for your contribution 

Godot 2.x is no longer supported, we do not accept general contributions to it

Thank you for the response. Is there a way to submit this fix? Should this be a proposal? Or let it go? I'm very new to contributing, I apologize. I'm stuck on 2.1 to support Android API 16 for the OUYA.

Edit: changed API 18 to API 16

You can always just fix this in your own fork

Though I'd be interested in why you would be using 2.1, it was discontinued a long time ago, last release was 8 years ago

> Thank you for your contribution
> 
> Godot 2.x is no longer supported, we do not accept general contributions to it

Not supported doesn't mean we don't accept contributions for it though. But it's not a priority for sure.
It does mean however that we won't plan to make new releases of the improvements in the `2.1` branch.

In particular contributions to ensure that the code can still build on modern toolchains are quite valuable IMO for game preservation, so that's very welcome.

The fix seems fine, but is it really sufficient to build Godot 2.1 on modern macOS? I don't have a system to test but at least here on Linux, I have other issues related to the Python version. Are you using an older Python 3, or Python 2?

> You can always just fix this in your own fork
> 
> Though I'd be interested in why you would be using 2.1, it was discontinued a long time ago, last release was 8 years ago

I have! Just hoped I'd finally be able to contribute something back.

The OUYA needs OpenGL 2 and Android API 16. Support for those never co-exist in Godot 3. I've tried to lower the minimum Android SDK in Godot 3 with no success.
That's an interesting use case! Thank you for the details

> The fix seems fine, but is it really sufficient to build Godot 2.1 on modern macOS? I don't have a system to test but at least here on Linux, I have other issues related to the Python version. Are you using an older Python 3, or Python 2?

Yup! Works fine here. I'm using Python 2.7.18. I usually use SCons 2.5.1 for godot-for-ouya, but it seems to work fine in SCons 4.8 too. I've tested building with this change on three modern Macs running macOS 15/Xcode 16 and one older Mac running macOS 12/Xcode 14.

Doesn't Xcode 16 default to C++17 if unspecified, like osxcross/Apple Clang seems to do in my cross-compilation toolchain?

> Interesting, for me (on Linux with osxcross, SCons 4.8.1 and Python 3.13.0) I first run into this issue:

>   File "/root/godot/platform/android/detect.py", line 5:
>     from distutils.version import LooseVersion
> ```

I ran into that too! distutils was removed in Python 3.12. I tried adding distutils manually, but, eventually, switched to Python 2.7.18. I never saw that second issue.

I can't find an official doc that says so, but I've found a few posts on StackOverflow and forums that say Apple Clang defaults to C++98 if none is specified. Here's the latest post where I see that: https://forums.developer.apple.com/forums/thread/746509

> The fix seems fine

Should I make this pull request 'Ready for review'?

I included your fix in #101040 so we can test and validate compatibility with modern toolchains all at once. Could you test that PR on macOS and confirm that it works fine?

Thanks for the contribution!

Building the engine is working fine on macOS, but it seems to have broken building the Android export template. Here's the error I'm getting:

```
scons: Reading SConscript files ...

NameError: global name 'LooseVersion' is not defined:

```

I have been using NDK 17.2.4988734.

Also, and maybe interestingly, this did break building the engine using Windows VS2015 x64 Native, but it's still working in x64 2022 and VS2015 x64 x86 Cross Tools.
